subject: List::Util/Scalar::Util shim parity checklist — 110 board rows across 21 files
description:
FIRST PASS SHIPPED s376: the dist's own 38 files went 319 ok / 120 not-ok →
**398 ok / 75 not-ok** (12→17 PASS, 5→2 FAIL).  Measurement command:
  tools/cpan-scoreboard.pl --jobs 8 --no-dist-lib ~/.cpan/build/Scalar-List-Utils-1.70-0
METHOD NOTE (cost s344 a wrong reading first time): the perl oracle for this
dist must run WITHOUT -I<dist>/lib — the dist's XS is unbuilt, so perl dies at
`use` and the file looks like a board artifact.

DONE s376 (lib/List/Util.pm, lib/Scalar/Util.pm, two new builtin:: primitives):
 - maxstr/minstr/reductions/sample/zip_shortest/mesh_longest/mesh_shortest
   implemented (were dying stubs)
 - zip returns ARRAYREFS, mesh flattens (both had been the flat list)
 - product() of no args is 1
 - head/tail: `($@)` prototype, both-ends clamping, "Not enough arguments"
 - uniq / uniqstr / uniqint / uniqnum separated by what they compare AND
   what they return; uniqnum keys on `pack "d"` (raw double)
 - $List::Util::RAND honoured by shuffle + sample
 - pairgrep / pairfirst scalar-context answers
 - one shared _need_code → perl's two error texts for all ten block-taking
   functions (t/undefined-block.t 0/18 → 18/18)
 - looks_like_number: Inf/Infinity/NaN, "0 but true", [0-9] not \d
   (MONGOLIAN DIGIT FIVE), overloaded objects answer on stringification
 - isdual / isvstring via new builtin::is_dual / builtin::is_vstring
LAYER RULING s377 (Ask 5, docs/fable-answers-s376.md §5): builtin:: is
BLESSED as the shim-dispatch seam for box-representation primitives (with
the three constraints in the ruling).  `readonly` → same seam when the
scalar storage fact exists; `prototype` introspection → CORE builtin, goes
in the runtime as the ordinary builtin, NOT the seam.

NEXT BATCH (s377 rulings + review findings — sized from data):
 - uniqnum HYBRID KEY (RULED s377 §6, measured): integer-valued args with
   |v| < 2^64 key as exact integer text; else `pack "d"`.  The range bound
   is load-bearing: integral NVs beyond 2^64 MUST stay pack "d" (15-digit
   stringification collapses distinct doubles).  Ship undef→0 OUTPUT
   coercion with it (row 15: `uniqnum undef` returns 0 in perl).  Buys
   rows 7/10/11/15 of uniqnum.t's six; row 14 stays behind #221; row 22
   (unnamed, in the $Config{ivsize} 1e17 block) re-measure after.
 - looks_like_number residue (s377 probe): perl accepts `nanq`/`nans`
   (quiet/signalling NaN); the shim's NaN alternative does not — one
   character class (`NaN[QS]?`).
 - CADENCE (Ask 8 ruling): any lib/ shim change makes the full sweep +
   this dist's files NON-OPTIONAL in the shipping session — corpus-diff
   never transpiles a shim.

REMAINING rows, every one a PARKED family — do NOT re-derive these:
 - refaddr.t 9, reftype.t 4, getmagic-once.t 4 → tie (#155) and
   REF-vs-SCALAR (#163)
 - scalarutil-proto.t 9, prototype.t 4 → prototype()/set_prototype
   introspection; needs the runtime prototype registry to answer for a
   CODE ref, not just for a name (runtime builtin per the s377 layer
   ruling, not the builtin:: seam)
 - weak.t 6 → weaken/isweak need real weak references
 - uniq.t 5, pair.t 5 → the "yields a warning" rows (#221) and pairgrep
   ALIASING of the caller's list (@_ aliasing, not-supported)
 - readonly.t 4 → a read-only flag on SCALAR storage; PCL has it for array
   STORAGE only (#159).  `readonly(1)` is true in perl because @_ aliases
   the constant.  Real box-model work, not a filler.
 - tainted.t 3 → no taint mode in PCL
 - openhan.t 3 → `ref($fh)` of a lexical filehandle is "" in PCL, "GLOB" in
   perl, and `fileno($string)` returns a number instead of undef, so the
   shim cannot discriminate a handle from a string
 - reduce.t 3, first.t 1, head-tail.t 2 (the eval-string rows),
   sample.t 2 + reductions.t 2 (DESTROY at scope exit, #198), dualvar.t 2,
   lln.t 1 (tied hash) → error text (#149) and the parked runtime items
 - exotic_names.t (1554 rows) + subname.t (21) are the `subname` family:
   PCL cannot rename a compiled CL closure (lib/Sub/Util.pm documents it).
   THE BIG PRIZE if a name registry ever lands — SIZED FIRST as #284 (USER
   s376), measure before starting.
activeForm: Working the List::Util shim parity checklist
